export.gpuFailed:
Export failed: it looks like your GPU was reset during the export.

This usually means the hardware encoder hung or Windows reset the graphics driver. Try one of: lower the export resolution (Settings), disable plate blur for this export, export a shorter time range using IN/OUT markers, or update your graphics driver.

If it keeps happening, open Settings → Diagnostics → Console Log Capture and send us the log. It includes the encoder and decoder details that support@teslacamviewer.com needs to look into it.

export.formatHint: Format used when exporting videos. MP4 (VP9) looks best, but iPhone, QuickTime and some video editors and social apps can't open it: use MP4 (H.264) for those. MP4 (H.264) can be the slowest: if your graphics card's H.264 encoder doesn't respond, the export switches to the software encoder and remembers that for next time.
export.privacyModeHint: Strip timestamp, GPS, location, and mini-map from exports
export.gpsTextHint: Burns the car's GPS position into exported videos and screenshots as text, next to the timestamp. Off by default so a shared video or picture doesn't show where you were. Clips without GPS data use the event's approximate location, marked with ~. Privacy mode always removes it.
export.speedLimitHint: Shows the posted speed limit from OpenStreetMap as a sign in exported videos and screenshots, like the live sign. Limits are looked up online when the export starts (for up to about 6 seconds) and kept for next time. Roads that couldn't be looked up show no sign, and the export tells you when that happened (for example when the map data server is busy). Privacy mode always removes it.
export.blurPlatesHint: AI-powered plate detection (~12MB model, cached after first use)
export.brandingHint: Display branding in the bottom banner of exported videos
export.qualityHint: Scales the export canvas. Full never downsamples; HD/Web cap but never upscale; Custom lets you pick (can upscale).
export.customHeightHint: Width is computed to preserve the layout's aspect ratio.
export.plateModelOnFirstExport: Model will download on first export

aiSearch.modelCached: The model is downloaded once and cached by your browser.
aiSearch.modelLarge: Quality: CLIP ViT-L/14 (~570 MB, more confident tags)
aiSearch.aboutClip: AI Search uses CLIP (OpenAI's Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) to match your natural-language queries against video frames. The model is loaded in your browser via Transformers.js and runs entirely on your GPU (or CPU if no WebGPU is available).
aiSearch.modelBase: Fast: CLIP ViT-B/32 (175 MB download, 3× faster)
aiSearch.motion: Motion-filtered: every scene change (slower, catches short events)
aiSearch.noWebCodecs: Your browser doesn't support WebCodecs, so indexing will use a slower fallback path.
aiSearch.private: No video or data ever leaves your computer.
aiSearch.intro: Find events by describing the scene ("parking garage", "night drive", "pedestrian walking"). Uses an on-device AI model.
aiSearch.aboutBest: Best for: scene types, locations, general objects. Weaker at: specific colors, fine attributes. If a search doesn't find what you expect, right-click the event and choose "Deep-index" to sample more frames.
aiSearch.samplingHint: You can "Deep-index" individual events on demand regardless of this default.
aiSearch.sparse: Sparse: 1 frame per clip (fast first run)
aiSearch.notSetUp: search is not set up yet
aiSearch.clearConfirm: Clear the AI search index? You'll need to re-index to search again.

encrypted.explain: Tesla software 2026.20 and newer encrypts dashcam clips on the USB drive. Only your car or your Tesla account can unlock them.
encrypted.webText: sign in with your Tesla account, decrypt and download the clips (it runs in your browser), then add the downloaded folder here with Add drive.
encrypted.carText: in the car's Dashcam viewer, tap the padlock on a clip. This decrypts it on the USB drive and can't be undone.
encrypted.stopText: {{path}} (not every car shows this setting). Clips that are already encrypted stay encrypted.
encrypted.stopPrivacy: Encryption keeps your footage private if someone gets your USB drive; turning it off means anyone with the drive can watch it.

welcome.title: Welcome to TeslaCam Viewer

step1.title: Step 1: Select Your TeslaCam Folder

step2.description: Events appear in the left sidebar, sorted by date. Click any event to load it.

step3.title: Step 3: View Cameras
step3.description: Watch all camera angles synchronized: Front, Back, Left, Right, and Pillar cameras (if available).

license.howItWorks: Here's how your TeslaCamViewer Pro license works:
license.privacyFirstDesc: Your email is only used to verify your license locally on this device. It's never sent to any server.
license.savedInTwoPlacesDesc: Your license is saved in your browser's storage and on your TeslaCam drive. This lets you use it across different drives.
license.easyRecoveryDesc: If you use a different browser or computer, just open any drive with your license saved on it. You'll be asked to re-enter your email to verify it's you.
license.multipleDevicesDesc: Use your license on any device. Each new browser will ask for your email once to verify, then you're all set.
license.limitDailyText: You've viewed {{limit}} events today. You can still open any of them again to keep exploring; only new events wait. The limit resets at midnight.
license.limitExportText: Free lets you export {{limit}} events a day: {{names}}. You can export those again as often as you like, and pick new ones after midnight. Pro removes the limit.
license.limitLockedText: This feature needs a TeslaCamViewer Pro license.

fileProtocol.notice: You opened TeslaCamViewer straight from its folder (file://), so your browser blocks some features: telemetry, license plate tools, MP4 and GIF exports, and translations. To use everything, open teslacamviewer.com, or start a local server in this folder (for example: python -m http.server 8000) and open http://localhost:8000.
